newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end mixed, electronics up.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end mixed, electronics up.

text.p: Singapore shares ended mixed on Friday with late buying seen in selected electronics and banking stocks.

Dealers said there was profit-taking in the wider market ahead of the weekend. "A lot of selling seen in Malaysian OTC stocks. Most people do not want to hold positions ahead of the Lunar New Year next week," said one broker.

But some buying was seen in electronics counters including Creative Technologies, Elec & Eltek, Wong's Circuits and Venture Manufacturing. Creative is expected to release a strong set of second quarter results over the weekend.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials index ended down 0.24 points at 2,216.47. Total market volume was 265 million with 213 losers outpacing 157 gainers.
Newly-listed electronics firm ASJ ended at S$0.845 cents, a premium of more than 60 percent over its offer price of S$0.52, with about 21 million units traded.
Topping the gainers list was SPH foreign which rose S$1.10 to S$28.20 with more than half a million shares changing hands. Other gainers included ST Capital and DBS foreign.
Keppel Corp, Cycle & Carriage, YHS and SIA foreign ended lower. - Doreen Siow (65-8703092)
